text: The account's logo goes in the header, beside the seller's logo: the template's `account_logo` slot, or `accountLogo` in the plain header.
Never put the account's logo anywhere else on the page.
A row of the seller's customer logos must not suggest the account is already a customer.

loc: 1. Start from the brand's own images
text: The brand's images are in `brand/brand.md`, each with a description. A description can be wrong or missing, so look at an image with `view_asset` before you use it.
Anything real comes only from these images: product screenshots, the seller's photos of its people and customers, logos, customer stories. Never generate them.
Check that the image fits the words beside it. A product screenshot must show what the copy says. A graphic with its own words baked in rarely fits a new heading.
The seller's other images (uploads, and images made for earlier pages) are not in `brand/brand.md`. Find them with `search_assets`, and look at one with `view_asset` before you use it.

loc: 2. Generate only a scene or a mood
text: Generate an image only when a section needs one and none of the brand's images fits.

A generated image may show a scene or a mood: a school-district setting for a school district, or an abstract background in the brand's colours. It must not show: words, numbers or logos; real people, or anyone presented as a real person; a product screen, or anything presented as the seller's product; anything presented as the account's own building, staff or customers.

To keep it in the brand's style, pass one to three of the brand's own photos as `style_references`, and ask for the shape the section needs. Look at the result. If it breaks a rule above or looks off-brand, try once more with a clearer prompt, or leave the image out.

loc: 3. No image beats a weak image
text: If nothing fits and a generated image would not help the reader, choose a section without an image.

If `brand/brand.md` has no logo for the account, or none fits the header, call `fetch_logo` with the account's website domain. Look at what it finds with `view_asset` before you place one. If it finds nothing, hide the account's logo and say so in your report.
Leave out a logo of a company with the same or a similar name as the account, or one that could be its parent or subsidiary.
